About

Peace of the heart, in Lingala: Kimia Na Motema.

A work inspired by the Lord Yehoshua (Jesus), carried by a group of Christians moved by the love of Elohim and by compassion for people in need.

The Christian association La Paix du Cœur / Kimia Na Motema is a work inspired by the Lord Yehoshua (Jesus), carried by a group of Christians moved by the love of Elohim and by compassion for people in need. We work humbly and selflessly, for the glory of Elohim alone.

Founded in Montréal, Canada, in 2014, the vision began as a way to bring support and hope to orphans. It has grown to include widows and widowers, the poor and the homeless — regardless of language, colour or race.

We ask nothing of the people we help. Everything is free.

Kimia
na
motema

Kimia means “peace” and motema means “heart”. The Lingala name remembers where the vision comes from; the French name says where it is rooted today: Montréal.

Commitment

Our ethical storytelling charter

An awareness campaign must never cost anyone their dignity. These are our commitments.

  1. 01Hope before need: we show the moment things turn around, never distress in close-up.
  2. 02No identifiable child’s face without written consent from a parent or guardian — and never a child alone on a cover.
  3. 03First names only, never an exact place.
  4. 04Everyone reviews their own story and can withdraw it at any time.
  5. 05Figures are checked; those not yet checked are marked “to confirm”.

Religion that is pure and undefiled before our Elohim and Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction…
